column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately forbids Israel going in among them and their going in among Israel; BSB combines this as not intermarrying. It uses singular “your heart,” where BSB uses plural “hearts.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that his heart was not whole with the LORD and repeats “heart” when comparing David; BSB says that he was not wholeheartedly devoted and leaves the final heart image implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the hill was “before Jerusalem”; BSB specifies “east of Jerusalem.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves Solomon unnamed in both clauses and calls the warning a command; BSB names him twice and uses “warned.”
The Hebrew says “this has been with you” and intensifies tearing by repeating the root; BSB says “you have done this” and uses a single tearing verb.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add the recipient “from him” to the first clause; BSB supplies it.
The Hebrew uses “seed of the king”; BSB renders this as “royal line.”
The Hebrew explicitly says that Joab went up to bury the slain; BSB leaves the upward direction implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names Hadad at both the beginning and the final description of the boy; BSB names him once and moves the boy description forward.
The Hebrew leaves the departing subjects unnamed and uses “bread”; BSB supplies “Hadad and his men” and “food.”
The Hebrew repeats “sister” in naming Pharaoh’s wife and Tahpenes; BSB combines these relationships into one phrase.
The Hebrew does not name Hadad in this verse and twice says “Pharaoh’s house”; BSB supplies Hadad, says “palace,” and replaces the second house reference with “there.”
The Hebrew repeats Hadad’s name and says “go” to his land; BSB uses “he” and “return.”
The Hebrew leaves Hadad unnamed and strengthens the sending-away verb by repetition; BSB names him and supplies “please.” BSB also adds “suddenly” to Pharaoh’s question.
The Hebrew uses a pronoun for the one opposed and says “an adversary”; BSB names Solomon and adds “another.”
The Hebrew uses a pronoun for those David killed and plural verbs for going to Damascus and reigning there; BSB supplies “the Zobaites,” names Rezon, and presents his going in the singular.
The Hebrew leaves Rezon unnamed; BSB names him twice.
The Hebrew says that he raised a hand against the king; BSB renders the image as rebelling.
The Hebrew repeats raising a hand against the king and names the Millo; BSB says “rebellion” and “supporting terraces.” BSB also supplies “in the wall” when describing the gap.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses pronouns for the man Ahijah met and the wearer of the new cloak; BSB explicitly names Jeroboam and Ahijah.
Close to the Hebrew.
